retention: Matched control for ADD-immediate lowering and gadget layout changes, sharing its body with the ideal gadget ceiling bench.
Private-counter control for direct atomic lowering and multicore scaling.
Guest CMP-immediate followed by B.cond, the shape a translated block ends on. The loop counters in the other probes are subs with a real destination and so never take the fused path.

Guest CMP of two registers followed by B.cond. G116 ranks this pair fourth and ninth over a full Geekbench run while the immediate form does not reach the table, so the two shapes get separate probes.
Private compare-and-retry control for exclusive sequence quality.
Exercises the shared load-result and store-status register fallback shape.
Measures floating-state activation and restoration overhead.
Measures a run of native floating-point operations sharing one program-level environment activation.
Measures vector-state successor linking through a conditional self-edge.
Stresses floating-state exits at a polymorphic indirect branch site.
Matched DC-CVAU execution-boundary control for exact gadget-cache validation without advancing the guest code-change sequence.
Uses IC IVAU on unchanged code every iteration to measure exact reuse of stale gadget programs after the guest code-change sequence advances.
Matched DC-CVAU control for the link-population probe: same chain walk and same execution boundary without advancing the guest code-change sequence.

Walks a chain of thousands of distinct single-branch blocks once so the link table carries a standing population, then runs the IC IVAU loop. The other invalidation probe names only a handful of targets, so it cannot measure how the link reset scales with translated code.
Cycles one ADD-immediate gadget's indirect dispatch through eight distinct successor gadget families to isolate G107's early-target-fetch hypothesis.
Matched DC-CVAU control for the reindex probe: same full-size block and execution boundary without advancing the guest code-change sequence, so no reactivation occurs.

Reactivates a full-size translated block every iteration so the stream index walk, which scales with program size rather than with guest work, is measurable. The other invalidation probes time a four-instruction block that spans one or two index granules.
Measures same-page scalar memory runs through an allocated base register.
Measures monomorphic indirect-call and return successor linking.
Matched control for in-place ADD-immediate lowering, interleaving three chains so no adjacent forward is selected and every word reaches its guest register through CpuState.

Matched control for unsigned-offset transfers whose transferred register is a baked CpuState displacement. Three load/modify/store chains run interleaved through one same-page buffer, so no adjacent forward is ever selected and every value crosses CpuState between the load that produced it and the store that consumes it.
Matched control for same-page native integer pair transfers.

ISB then MRS CNTVCT_EL0, the counter read of arm64 Linux's vDSO without FEAT_ECV. The only probe that runs an ISB, so the only one that measures the code-change sequence check both engines make at a context synchronization point.
Baseline for cached direct successor-link throughput.
Matched control for logical-register move alias lowering.

Maps an anonymous region, faults in and checks every page, and unmaps it, as allocators and loaders return memory. Measures publishing and removing host mappings and the software TLB range invalidation an unmap causes.
Measures repeated scalar and vector accesses at stable translated sites.

Walks four times the software TLB's capacity from threads sharing one address space, so every access is a miss and the software-MMU translate path is measured under the concurrency the multi-core phase produces.
MOVK at every halfword position and EXTR at both widths plus the ROR alias, in the loop body. The other integer probes reach these entries only while materialising their iteration count.
Measures translation-predecoded scalar operand addressing.

The ADRP plus ADD address idiom in a loop. G113 measured it as the third most frequent adjacent gadget pair in translated code, and the other probes use it once each on their way out rather than in a loop.
Rotates one BLR site through thirty-two targets, more than any site's cells hold, as virtual calls and handler dispatch do. Pairs with guest_indirect_link_loop.S as the monomorphic control.
Exercises the software reservation fallback followed by publication.
Exercises the bounded native reservation sequence followed by publication.

A parent and a forked child pinned to one CPU hand a byte back and forth over pipes and each touch a small working set, so every hand-off switches one vCPU's software TLB between address spaces. The only probe whose cost is the TLB flush and refill a context switch causes.
Matched control for the page-contained scalar byte fast path.

Realistic scalar mix (loads, stores, pairs, narrow accesses, flag-setting ALU, selects, a never-taken check and two data-dependent skips) sharing its body with the ideal gadget ceiling bench and printing the checksum, path counts and retired instructions the host bench must reproduce.
Measures basic vector floating arithmetic register addressing.
Matched out-of-bank control for the destination-resident integer MLA run.
Measures a 32-instruction integer MLA run with one repeated v0 destination and nonaliasing sources.
Measures indexed vector multiply-add register addressing.

Realistic FP/SIMD mix (vector pair and register-offset transfers, indexed and vector FMLA, converts, an FP compare branch) sharing its body with the ideal gadget ceiling bench and printing the checksum, path counts and retired instructions the host bench must reproduce.
Measures signed pairwise-add-long vector lowering.
Measures signed widening-multiply vector lowering.
Measures one-register structure transfers with remapped vector state.
Two-table control for one-table lookup specialization changes.
Measures one-table vector lookup operand addressing.
Measures same-width three-register vector addition lowering.
Measures same-page unsigned-offset vector memory runs.
Measures adjacent scalar memory runs addressed directly from SP.

Repeated getpid, the cheapest syscall the guest kernel offers, so the loop measures the guest entry boundary rather than the work behind it. The only probe that exercises the per-entry thread execution state resolution.

Load-acquire through a top-byte-tagged pointer beside a plain load of the same page, as a tagged heap object read both ways, and both use the read half of the page's TLB entry. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control. Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

LSE atomic through a top-byte-tagged pointer beside a plain store to the same page, and both use the write half of the page's TLB entry. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control. Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

LSE atomic through a top-byte-tagged pointer alone on its page, the cost of the form itself. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control (guest_atomic_add_loop.S is the untagged single-instruction loop). Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

Load-acquire through a top-byte-tagged pointer alone on its page, the cost of the ordered form itself. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control. Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

SIMD&FP transfers through a top-byte-tagged pointer with the tagged-address ABI enabled, as every Android process with heap pointer tagging makes them. The other vector memory probes use untagged addresses.
Detects regressions in the 4 KiB TLB's index width: two pages half the table's reach apart take separate entries.
Matched control for same-page native vector pair transfers.

Executes five fixed-work samples of 160 million STR S register-offset stores selecting vector_other_store32_x_0, matched instruction-for-instruction with the unsigned-offset probe for cross-host comparison.

Executes five fixed-work samples of 160 million STR S unsigned-offset stores selecting vector_store32_unsigned_fast, matched instruction-for-instruction with the register-offset probe for cross-host comparison.
Contended spin lock whose backoff uses the YIELD hint. The only probe in which a guest thread waits on another, so the only one able to measure guest YIELD lowering.
